Buying back pension service: compare the payment calendar with the additional pension

Four charts compare an upfront payment with quoted monthly deductions, the wait before pension receipt and the effect of different receipt horizons.

By TickerLantern Research · Published 25 October 2026 · 5 min read
Sources reviewed 25 October 2026

Change an assumption. Follow the result.

Compare independently quoted buyback payments and pension increases

Interactive planning lab

Total quoted monthly deductions$42,000
Upfront option: incremental present value$15,556.06
Instalment option: incremental present value$10,870.18

Hypothetical gross cash comparison from the election date, assuming both fully completed payment options buy the same separately quoted additional pension. Upfront cost is paid now; deductions begin at month one. Pension payments begin at the end of month (waiting years × 12 + 1), rise once after each twelve payments, and continue for thirty receipt years conditional on survival. Monthly discounting uses the effective annual nominal rate. All scheduled deductions fit inside this full horizon. Quoted deductions are entered directly, not derived from a loan rate. No tax deduction, PSPA, RRSP transfer, eligibility, bridge-benefit change, survivor benefit, death probability, refund, investment alternative or plan approval is calculated. Present value is conditional cash arithmetic, not actuarial value or a recommendation.

The central idea

The buyback price, payment timing and additional pension answer different questions. Use matched plan quotes, then examine the cash commitment and conditional benefit stream.

01

Start with the plan’s quote, not a generic pension formula

A service buyback purchases recognition of eligible prior service under a particular pension plan. Whether it is available, what it costs and how it changes benefits must come from that plan. The model does not infer eligibility or turn years worked into a pension amount.

For the federal public service plan, Treasury Board’s explanation describes a legally binding agreement and payment choices including a lump sum, monthly deductions or a combination. These rules do not establish the terms of another employer’s plan.

Ask for a comparison of benefits with and without the proposed buyback, at the same retirement date. Confirm the effect on eligibility, temporary benefits, indexing and survivor provisions. Enter only an independently quoted incremental monthly pension; this tool assumes it can be represented by one starting amount and an annual increase.

02

A smaller monthly deduction can add up to a larger nominal payment

The default alternatives are CAD 30,000 paid immediately or CAD 350 deducted monthly for ten years. The latter totals CAD 42,000 across 120 deductions. The first chart makes that total visible.

The federal explanation says its monthly deductions include principal, interest and life-insurance amounts. It also describes protection associated with life-insured instalments. A real quote’s additional charges and protections need to be assessed together; a comparison of payment totals alone cannot value them.

The tool accepts the monthly quote directly. It does not calculate an interest rate, insurance premium, outstanding buyback loan or death settlement. Both options are assumed to buy the same additional pension after their commitments are fulfilled. A quote offering different service or benefits would need a different comparison.

03

Draw the years when you pay but do not yet receive the increase

The example waits ten years before the first pension receipt year begins. Monthly pension payments then start at the end of month 121. The first twelve are CAD 250 each, a gross CAD 3,000 over that first receipt year.

The upfront line begins at negative CAD 30,000 at year zero. The instalment line begins at zero and falls as deductions are paid. Both later receive the same modeled pension increase. Annual points summarize a monthly ledger, with no hidden return on the money retained under either option.

Shorten the wait while keeping the deduction term unchanged and payments can overlap pension receipts. The ledger continues subtracting them. An annual positive change does not establish that all intra-year household bills can be funded; this is incremental buyback cash, not a full bank-account schedule.

04

Specify when indexing begins and what the pension amount includes

The default pension increase grows by an assumed 2% after every twelve payments. The second receipt year therefore pays CAD 255 per month. No increase is applied during the ten-year wait because the input is explicitly the quoted amount for the first receipt year.

If a plan quote is expressed in today’s dollars or already incorporates an indexing estimate, reconcile that basis before entering it. Applying an extra increase to a quote that already includes it would double count. Likewise, a temporary bridge component cannot be assumed to continue indefinitely.

All benefits and payment costs here are gross cash amounts. The illustration excludes deductions, tax relief, changes to contribution room, past service pension adjustments and transfers from registered savings. A tax deduction or direct transfer should not be assumed to be freely available cash.

05

Bring both payment schedules and the pension receipts to the election date

The third chart discounts each monthly amount to the date of the decision. Its payment bars differ because CAD 30,000 now and CAD 350 spread over ten years have different timing. Its benefit bars match because both options receive the same pension stream by assumption.

Subtract the payment present value from the pension present value to reconcile each headline result. At a zero discount rate, this is simply total gross pension receipts less the relevant nominal payment total. With a positive rate, a later receipt has less present weight.

A positive conditional present value is not an actuarial valuation or an instruction to buy. The tool does not compare an invested portfolio, attach probabilities to future payments or value protection on death. The appropriate comparison rate itself requires judgment and cannot turn contingent income into certain cash.

06

Test the receipt horizon without pretending it predicts survival

The main comparison shows thirty pension receipt years after the selected wait. The matrix separately tests ten, twenty and thirty receipt years for the upfront option, alongside three starting monthly increases. Those are chosen horizons, not life-expectancy estimates or probability bands.

A shorter receipt horizon reduces the modeled benefit stream while leaving the upfront cost unchanged. A longer wait also places the same future receipts farther from the election date. These two timing effects are distinct and can be explored separately.

The model assumes the member survives throughout the selected receipt period, then ends the calculation. It does not model a death event, refund, survivor pension or estate payment. Those omissions make a personal plan quote and its protection terms essential before interpreting the result as a complete economic comparison.

07

Check the agreement and the household cash capacity together

Before acting, obtain the current written cost, expiry date, eligible service, payment schedule and benefit comparison from the administrator. Resolve any medical conditions, tax certification, deadlines and cancellation restrictions with the plan. The charts do not confirm any of them.

Separately, check how an upfront payment affects emergency cash and nearer goals, and how payroll deductions fit the working-year budget. A pension increase later cannot pay an unrelated bill today. Registered money transferred to a pension is also money no longer available in its former account.

A useful decision combines verified plan terms, an affordable funding method and a retirement-income plan. This article provides a transparent gross cash comparison; it does not replace the plan’s calculations or recommend electing an agreement.

Sources and scope

Public sources reviewed on 25 October 2026. Charts labelled “Official statistics” or “Derived from official statistics” identify their source periods. Other charts are hypothetical scenarios. Original scenario calculations and research checklists are TickerLantern’s educational analysis; attributed publisher examples retain their stated source and scope. Recheck current issuer documents for any product-specific decision.

  1. Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat · Increasing your public service pension ↗

    Live official page reviewed 25 October 2026. Supports the federal plan’s buyback definition, payment options and the presence of interest/life-insurance costs in monthly deductions. It does not supply the hypothetical quote or determine another plan’s rules.

  2. Government of Canada Pension Centre · Estimates and service buyback ↗

    Reviewed 25 October 2026 for the role of the Pension Centre in cost estimates, benefit impact, payments and tax information. No administrative deadline or entitlement is encoded in this model; use the current member package and individual quote before an election.
